title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B as it looks to take drug candidates to clinical trials
content:
Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-discovery platform that was spun out of Google’s DeepMind in 2021, has raised $5 billion in a Series C funding round as it seeks to take its drug candidates to clinical trials.
The funding was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with new investor Andreessen Horowitz and other investors also participating. All of the company’s existing backers, including Alphabet’s venture divisions GV and Capital G, Thrive Capital, MGX, Temasek, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund, also invested.
Isomorphic Labs builds an AI drug-design engine that uses a slew of simulation AI models that explore various areas of chemistry to help the company design drugs. The company, whose work builds on DeepMind’s breakthrough AlphaFold protein-folding AI model, said its program has yielded “positive preclinical results” in oncology and immunology. The lab has struck deals with pharma giants like Eli Lilly, Novartis, and Johnson & Johnson.
The new funding, which comes on the heels of a $2.1 billion Series B round in May, will be used to continue developing its drug-design engine, as well as to foray into more types of medicine.
The Series C is Isomorphic’s first fundraise since its founder and CEO, Demis Hassabis, left his position as head of DeepMind to focus on drug discovery, which also saw him moving into a chairman role at DeepMind. Hassabis and then-director of DeepMind John Jumper won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for the lab’s work on AlphaFold, a system that predicts the 3D structure of proteins with nothing more than their genetic sequence.
Isomorphic did not disclose its new valuation. Bloomberg reported earlier this month that the lab was looking to raise funding at a $50 billion valuation.

report.summary: Isomorphic Labs raised $5B in Series C to push its AI-designed drug candidates into clinical trials after positive preclinical results.
report.background: Isomorphic Labs spun out of Google DeepMind in 2021 to apply AI to drug discovery. Its work builds on AlphaFold, DeepMind's breakthrough model for predicting protein 3D structures from genetic sequences, which earned Demis Hassabis and John Jumper a Nobel Prize in chemistry. Drug discovery is notoriously slow and expensive, with high failure rates and long development timelines. Pharma companies are increasingly partnering with AI labs to compress early discovery and improve candidate selection. Isomorphic has already signed deals with Eli Lilly, Novartis, and Johnson & Johnson. The new round follows a $2.1B Series B in May and comes as Hassabis shifted from DeepMind CEO to chairman there to focus on drug discovery.
key_points: Isomorphic Labs raised $5 billion in a Series C round co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with Andreessen Horowitz joining as a new investor. Existing backers including Alphabet's GV and Capital G, Thrive Capital, MGX, Temasek, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund also participated. The company did not disclose its valuation, though Bloomberg reported it was targeting $50 billion.

The company says its AI drug-design engine has produced positive preclinical results in oncology and immunology. The platform uses multiple simulation AI models that explore chemistry spaces to design drug candidates. The new capital will fund continued development of that engine and expansion into more types of medicine as Isomorphic moves toward clinical trials.

Pharma partnerships give Isomorphic both validation and real-world testing ground. Deals with Eli Lilly, Novartis, and Johnson & Johnson signal that large drugmakers are willing to embed AI discovery platforms in their pipelines. These collaborations could help translate computational designs into candidates that pass experimental and eventually clinical hurdles.

The raise is the first since founder Demis Hassabis left the DeepMind CEO role to concentrate on drug discovery and became DeepMind chairman. Hassabis and John Jumper won the Nobel Prize for AlphaFold, the protein-structure prediction system underpinning Isomorphic's approach. The funding reflects investor confidence in that scientific lineage.
report.impact: The raise is a strong signal that investors see AI drug discovery as more than research hype. A $5B round, even before clinical proof, gives Isomorphic unusual firepower to build wet-lab capacity, fund trials, and expand into new therapeutic areas. For the AI industry, it validates deep-tech spinouts from major labs and pressures competitors to show preclinical and clinical milestones, not just model benchmarks. For developers, it highlights demand for skills in structural biology, generative chemistry, simulation, and ML engineering, though proprietary data and lab validation remain barriers. For regular users, the payoff would be faster development of new medicines, but clinical trials take years and most candidates fail. Patients should expect gradual progress, not immediate treatments.
report.tools: To follow the space, watch AlphaFold Protein Structure Database for predicted structures, OpenFold for open-source protein folding, Boltz-2 and Chai-1 for open biomolecular structure prediction, and DiffDock for AI docking. Isomorphic's own engine is not public, but its pharma partnerships and publications are worth tracking.
